title: Floquet scattering and Fano resonances in nodal-ring and multi-Weyl semimetals: Role of propagating and evanescent modes
abstract: We develop a comprehensive Floquet scattering theory for quantum transport in periodically driven nodal-ring semimetals (NRSs) and multi-Weyl semimetals (mWSMs), extending our earlier study reported in Annalen der Physik 535, 2200460 (2023), in which evanescent modes were neglected, to a complete formalism that includes both propagating and evanescent channels. By solving the full boundary-value problem, we obtain the complete set of scattering states and show that, although evanescent modes are indispensable for satisfying the matching conditions at the potential interfaces, they carry zero net probability current and do not contribute to any observable transport quantity. We identify a previously unexplored transport regime in NRSs in which two propagating channels coexist and participate in coherent scattering, producing multi-channel quantum interference and Floquet-induced Fano resonances. The transmission, reflection, pumped shot noise, and the associated Fano resonance features are determined entirely by the propagating channels, and the resonance energies coincide with those of the corresponding quasi-bound states of the static potential well. Our results establish a unified framework for Floquet transport in anisotropic topological semimetals, and confirm that the approximation of neglecting evanescent modes in our earlier work is justified for all measurable transport properties.
summary: This work extends Floquet scattering theory to analyze quantum transport in topological semimetals like nodal-ring and multi-Weyl systems under periodic driving. By solving the full boundary problem, the authors prove that while evanescent modes are required for mathematical consistency, only propagating modes dictate observable transport properties. This establishes a unified framework for understanding Floquet-induced phenomena like Fano resonances in these complex materials.
main_problem: The paper develops a comprehensive Floquet scattering theory to analyze quantum transport in periodically driven nodal-ring and multi-Weyl semimetals.
main_result: It establishes that while evanescent modes are mathematically necessary for boundary matching, they do not contribute to measurable transport quantities like transmission or shot noise, which are determined entirely by propagating channels.
method: The authors solve the full boundary-value problem using Floquet scattering theory, constructing the scattering matrix by matching wavefunctions and their derivatives at potential interfaces.
model_or_system: The study focuses on Nodal-Ring Semimetals (NRSs) and multi-Weyl Semimetals (mWSMs) subjected to a time-periodic driving potential. The analysis involves solving the time-dependent Schrödinger equation in the Floquet basis.
key_observables: Transmission, reflection, pumped shot noise, and Floquet-induced Fano resonance features.
important_parameters: The driving frequency ($\omega$), the potential strength ($V_0, V_1$), and the topological nature of the semimetals (NRSs, mWSMs).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the zero-temperature limit for shot noise calculations and relies on the mathematical necessity of including evanescent modes for consistency in nonlinear dispersion regimes.

paper_structure: The paper builds from developing the full Floquet scattering formalism for anisotropic topological semimetals, deriving the scattering matrix by solving boundary conditions across interfaces, and finally analyzing the resulting transport coefficients and Fano resonance signatures.
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical treatment of boundary conditions in the presence of time-periodic driving and complex band structures (Weyl/Nodal-Ring) provides a powerful, general framework for analyzing open quantum systems dynamics.
